problem: Two triangles with two corresponding angles equal and either their included side or a side opposite one equal angle equal have the remaining sides and angle equal.

proof_idea.original: Treat both side placements; exclude unequal corresponding sides by cutting a side, SAS, and an exterior-angle contradiction.
proof_idea.analytic_included: Angle congruence gives determinant-square/norm-product ratios. Their common positive scale relates both unknown side squares; cosine numerators at the fixed base endpoints sum to its squared length, so its square-root scale must equal 1. SSS gives the remaining angle.
proof_idea.analytic_opposite: Apply the existing independently established analytic AAS theorem to a permuted triangle, then SSS for the remaining angle.
